    • stepScan

      private void stepScan(int writers) throws IOException
      Scan maven index files and write them to the database in batches.

      Pipeline (Java 24+ stream gatherers, JEP 485): 

        chunks → raw records (seq assigned) → windowFixed(batchSize)
         → mapConcurrent(converters, convertBatch) → mapConcurrent(writers + 1, storeBatch)
      Reading and decoding the index is sequential and runs on this thread, which also assigns the record sequence in index order. Expanding records, building documents and preparing SQL rows is about two thirds of the CPU work, so it runs on converters virtual threads. mapConcurrent keeps the input order, so batches still reach the writers in sequence order.

      Why writers + 1 tasks plus writerPermits: mapConcurrent blocks the scanning thread whenever all of its task slots are busy. With exactly writers slots, the next batch could only be handed over after a write finished, leaving a writer idle; for SQLite (one writer) converting and writing would not overlap at all. The extra slot holds one ready batch that waits for a permit, so the writers stay busy. With one writer this also keeps the SQLite writes in sequence order.

      Memory: at most converters + writers + 3 batches (being filled, converting, writing, one ready). A failed batch throws out of this method; the other in-flight batches are cancelled.

      Parameters:
      writers - Maximum number of batches written at the same time
      Throws:
      IOException - Failed to read the index
